note: Coverage gap, declared rather than patched. The measured layout boxes 24 regions on 15 of the 26 pages, and only 12 of those regions are exhibits: 7 figures and 5 tables. The rest are pasted equation blocks (pages 12, 13, 14 are each a single page-sized screenshot of prose plus display mathematics, and equations 28, 29 and 30 are separate smaller pastes). Several tables were never boxed at all, because they are native text-layer columns rather than images: Table 2 (Office Locations, p19) and Tables A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in the appendix. Of those, A3, A4 and A7 happen to fall inside regions that the layout did box (p24 and p25), so the three entries recorded here are the continuation rows and the final table of a longer appendix run; the remaining five appendix tables and Table 2 are recorded nowhere in this payload and are known to exist. Any aggregation of table shapes from this record should be read as 'the five boxed tables', not 'the paper's tables'. Two further cautions for anyone reusing these fields. First, four regions each hold TWO separately numbered figures pasted into one embedded image (Figures 3+4 on p16, 5+6 and 7+8 on p17, 9+10 on p18), so one region carries one composite-panel item and the printed numbers outrun the region count. Second, those caption lines are physically unreliable: on p16 and p18 the two captions run together on one printed line with no separator, and on p17 the pair collides ('Proportions inFigure 6') and wraps a stray '2068' onto the following line, so a caption-to-panel mapping taken from line adjacency will mis-assign; the left/right position on the page is the only safe key. The two schematics (Figures 1 and 2) are pasted raster exports with no axes, no legend and no unit, and their encodings are inline arrow labels; Figure 2's caption is the only thing that says which nation is which. Table 1's caption lives inside its screenshot and never reaches the text layer, so it is transcribed from the crop and marked typed-from-crop; the same is true of the notations table's absent title.
rules: Caption side is decided by kind, not by fit: every figure is captioned below the artwork (7 of 7) and every boxed table above it (5 of 5), so a reader never has to look twice for the label. [caption.position]

This paper always prints the colon form - 'Figure 2:', 'Table 1:' - on both kinds, and the colon is the only numbering style present, so the extractor's colonless 'Figure N' should be treated as a stale default here. [caption.numbering]

Five of the seven figures are composite-panel, because the authors pasted two separately numbered figures into a single embedded image rather than laying out two objects; the census must therefore count printed numbers, not regions. [geometry.panel_count]

Every panel pair is laid out side by side, never stacked, and where a panel has a key it keeps its own, so a pair is read as one exhibit with two independent axes rather than one continuous series. [geometry.family]

The legend never floats free of the artwork: it sits inside the image under the x axis on the three chart pairs, below the whole strip on Figure 11, and is absent with no substitute on the two schematics and on the map pair. [geometry.legend]

Nothing in this paper is three-dimensional - every exhibit is a flat area, rank line, choropleth or hand-drawn schematic - confirmed on the page crops rather than assumed from the family. [geometry.three_d]
No caption names a variable, states a unit, gives a condition or draws a conclusion: captions are bare 'what + where/when' noun phrases throughout. [caption.variables]
The year is the only quantity a chart caption ever carries, and it is the only place the horizon is stated; axes carry no title, so the year in the caption is load-bearing. [caption.words]
All five boxed tables share one recipe: horizontal rules only, no vertical divider, which makes the columns read as flowing prose blocks rather than a grid. [table.rule_style]
Continuation fragments keep no header and no caption of their own - the appendix tables that cross a page boundary resume as bare rows. [table.continued]
No table uses zebra striping, merged cells or a diagonal header, so a wide numeric table is disambiguated by rule position alone. [table.zebra]

Header rows are minimal: the fitting-result table prints no headings at all and the notations table prints exactly one, so the recorded header row is the minimum the schema allows rather than what the eye sees. [table.header_rows]

The two kinds occupy disjoint territories: figures live in the model, result and sensitivity sections, tables in the symbols, model and appendix sections, and neither kind appears in the introduction, the assumptions or the conclusion. [place.section_kind]

Five of the seven figures are cited by number and three of those pointers are on an earlier page than the artwork; the two that are never cited are the two schematics, which are self-explanatory by design. [mention.first_page]

Pre-figure pointers prefer naming the exhibit inside a running sentence ('Figure 3 and figure 4 indicates ...') over a parenthetical or a bare cross-reference, and the parenthetical is reserved for the rank pair. [mention.lead_pattern]

Two of the five cited charts are never interpreted in prose; the other three get between two and three reading sentences each, so half of this paper's chart space carries no written reading. [mention.read_sentences]

No table in the paper is ever cited by number - not the captioned Table 2, not the eight appendix tables - so a table number here is a label for the reader's eye, not a cross-reference target. [mention.style]
Post-figure prose sits immediately after the caption line with no blank-paragraph buffer, so a context weld has to key on the caption, not on vertical whitespace. [place.page_order]
Every exhibit is part of a page, never alone on one, and the largest occupies well under half the sheet, so no exhibit here earns a page of its own. [place.solo_page]

The unboxed tables are the census's real gap: Table 2 and the appendix tables are native text-layer columns that never became a region, so boxed-count alone would under-state the paper's tables by a factor of two. [place.area_frac]
